top.title: Frazier steps up to lift Indian Hill girls soccer to DIII state title
top.description: COLUMBUS, Ohio – Indian Hill’s girls soccer team relied on defense all year, but the Braves had several players who could step up and score goals when needed. In the team’s final game, it was Claire Frazier’s turn. The Indian Hill junior scored both goals for the Braves as they defeated Bay Village Bay 2-1 in the Ohio High School Athletic Association Division III girls soccer state championship game Nov. 14 at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field, the home of the Columbus Crew. Indian Hill finishes 19-0-4 and won its third state championship, first since 2018. The Braves shut out the Rockets (21-3), who had won the previous two state titles in Division III. Head coach Amy Dunlap picked up her 382nd career win. She has a 382-116-71 career record, leading the program to its eighth regional championship and now its third state title. “Just so incredibly proud of this team,” Dunlap said. “They’re resilient, they’re relentless and they just refuse to lose. And where we were when these kids came in four years ago, and then to end their senior year with the state championship, could not be any more exciting.” Frazier led the way, scoring both goals and ending the night with a team-high 11 for the season. Senior Kaylee VanDemark sparked both scoring plays. In the fifth minute, VanDemark fired a hard shot that the keeper couldn’t control. Frazier pounced on the rebound and tapped it in. In the 47th minute, VanDemark dribbled in space down the left side and crossed the ball past two opponents to Frazier, who had open space and scored from about eight yards out. “I know Claire’s always going to put her body on the line for the team,” VanDemark said. “She works really hard. Her dedication is unmatchable. I knew I could take (my) player on, so I took her on. I knew (Claire) was going to finish it because she puts everything on the line out there. It was amazing and I was so proud of her." Frazier is one of six players with five goals or more for the Braves. She was in the best form of the group this week, scoring one of the team’s goals in the state semifinals, a 2-1 win over Bexley. Senior Allie McCauley had the other and was second on the team with nine goals. They didn’t get many chances against a Rockets defense that conceded only 16 goals coming in, but they made them count. Indian Hill had 10 shots, six on goal. “I think they’re well-disciplined,” Bay head coach Scott Simpson said. “They play well. They play on the back well. They were calm and composed. Technically I thought they were pretty solid. They didn't have a lot of bad touches. That's one of the triggers you have for pressing things if you take bad touches and lose possession. I thought they were pretty consistent there.” The Braves nearly shut out a Rockets team that had scored 106 goals for the season and had five players in double figures. top.title: Pulisic Scores Twice As USMNT Crushes Haiti 6-0
top.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images Christian Pulisic scored two goals in just two minutes to push the United States men’s national team to a dominant 6-0 victory over Haiti on Saturday night. The win came in Miami during the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, marking the biggest rout of Mauricio Pochettino’s two years leading the squad. This result sets up a formality for the return leg in Cincinnati on Tuesday, where the current coach will take charge for the very last time. The buildup to this series carried heavy weight because Pochettino is leaving after only three months of a new four-year contract to become the manager of Manchester United, according to ESPN . Players showed no signs of distraction despite the looming change in leadership. Auston Trusty, who scored the opening goal from a corner kick in the 10th minute, spoke to TNT about the team’s focus on their departing coach. “We played for him,” Trusty told TNT. “Obviously he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. Obviously it’s a great opportunity that he is moving on into, but we play for him. It’s his team, it’s his identity.” Trusty also noted that the mindset remains to win every single game and keep fighting no matter how large the lead becomes. Pulisic returned to action for the first time since suffering an injury during a round-of-16 exit at the World Cup. Fourth on the team’s all-time leading scorers list, he surpassed Eric Wynalda thanks to his two second-half strikes. Five goals followed in a one-sided second half, with Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun rounding out the scoring alongside a fourth goal from teenager Julian Hall. Hall netted his fourth goal in just five appearances, a game that officially cap-tied him to the U.S. after he was previously eligible to represent Poland. A Final Sendoff in Miami Haiti was technically the home team for Saturday match, but the fixture moved to Miami due to ongoing gang violence in the Caribbean nation. The U.S. players executed a plan that left the opposition with little chance to respond, proving that the team can perform at a high level even when the coaching future remains uncertain. Next March, the Nations League semifinals and final are set to occur, with the U.S. under a yet-to-be-named new coach. While the team celebrates this massive win, attention shifts quickly to the search for the next leader. The United States Soccer Federation is reportedly pursuing Pep Guardiola aggressively, as initial negotiations are anticipated to begin next week. Since resigning as Manchester City’s manager in May 2026, Guardiola has been a highly-coveted free agent after securing 41 trophies over his 19 years managing in Europe. He reportedly turned down an offer of $11 million per season from Italy to take a year off. top.title: Lincoln Riley drives USC insane with another loss. It's time to pull plug | Opinion
top.description: What's the defintion of insanity? Well, it's Southern California. Because the Trojans keep doing the same thing over and over, expecting different results. In a result that has become an annual tradition, No. 14 USC lost another ranked game in November that has spoiled its hopes of the College Football Playoff . The 2026 edition of coach Lincoln Riley's tenure featured another mistake-riddled affair, blowing it against Indiana in a 27-13 loss . Riley is now just 6-15 in ranked games with the Trojans, including 1-9 on the road with the lone victory coming in his first season in 2022. Feeling insane yet? No matter how much talent he acquires or how the table is set perfectly for him, Riley continuously falls short in the games he not only is expected to win, but has to. No one cares he is 36-6 when facing unranked teams. When you're at USC, you're supposed to win the big games, and when you don't, that's when it's time for the bags to start being packed. USC was facing an Indiana team that hasn't been able to move the ball for over a month, and let backup quarterback Grant Wilson − making his first start since he was at Old Dominion in 2024 − throw for 305 yards and two touchdowns, opening up a battle at quarterback for the Hoosiers. It was the most points Indiana had scored since early October. Indiana has one of the best defenses in the country, but the loaded Trojans offense was meant to break it down just like how it did against Ohio State. Instead, USC was limited to just 13 points, and with Jayden Maiava throwing a season-high three interceptions, including in the red zone as the Trojans were on the cusp of tying the game late in the fourth quarter. USC also had both of its kickers miss a field goal. Once again, Riley's team completely implodes when the light at brightest. USC earned some credit back when it beat Ohio State on Halloween night , but that wasn't the end of it. Riley had to finally prove he could win those battles on the road, and instead he lost his eighth in a row. What may drive you even crazier is how after each defeat, Riley insists his team was "this close" to winning, forgetting being close only counts in horseshoes and hand grenades. However, a hand grenade just went off on USC's season. While not mathematically out of it just yet, 7-3 USC can kiss its CFP hopes goodbye just like its done every season under its coach, still yet to make the field since the playoff's inception in 2014. After consistently falling short, maybe that's why Riley was vocal about his desire to expand it to 24-teams, that way he can finally feel a sense of validation when he's able to win eight or nine games in a season. Oh, and that team across town is one win away from getting there before it does. top.title: How Ball State gave DePauw and Wabash another successful Monon Bell game
top.description: MUNCIE — In a game defined by the defenses, it was only fitting that the 132nd edition of the Monon Bell Classic came down to a clutch interception. With nine seconds left on the clock, Wabash quarterback Jackson Gilbert took the snap, dropped back, and launched a pass to the back left corner of the end zone for wide receiver Luke Adams. DePauw defensive back Joey Fico was there, though, and he leapt high into the air to snag the interception and seal a 16-10 victory for the Tigers at Ball State's Scheumann Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. "We've been practicing it all week," Fico said. "Not the pick, but the coverages. We knew that (Adams) was their guy, we got into a deep-third coverage, I saw him lined up one-on-one across from me. Their guy on our guy, I knew the ball was going to come up, and I was like, 'It's got to be me.' "I got up, did what I did, and the rest is history." As Fico came crashing down to the turf, the raucous crowd of DePauw fans and students that had filled up Ball State's bleachers erupted with thunderous cheers as the Tigers clinched their fifth-straight win over their archrival Little Giants. "You can't go to any other D-III school like Wabash and DePauw and get the support you get," Fico said. "I want to say a big thanks to all my friends and family that showed up because it does mean something. I definitely do play harder when there's a bunch of people out in front, knowing that they're supporting me." The Monon Bell Classic is not just the best Division III college football rivalry. It is considered by many to be the greatest rivalry the sport has to offer, no matter what level, and is one of the most historic rivalries in all of American sports, dating all the way back to 1890. With the two schools located just 27 miles apart in western Indiana — Wabash in Crawfordsville and DePauw in Greencastle — the rivaling rosters are often composed of high school teammates or even relatives. More: DePauw outlasts Wabash in 132nd Monon Bell game | Final score, highlights The Monon Bell itself — a 300-pound locomotive bell taken from the Monon Railroad — was introduced as a traveling trophy in 1932 and has famously been stolen by students from each school on nine different occasions. The famous Bell made its way through the procession of DePauw tailgaters that flooded the Scheumann Stadium parking lot before the game, and DePauw staffers and students rang it loudly and proudly before, during and after the game. How Ball State became the host for the 2026 Monon Bell Classic From 1915 until 1922, the rivalry game was held at neutral sites to accommodate larger crowds and alumni. The 1922 meeting at Irwin Field in Indianapolis marked the last time that the game was played at a neutral site until this year's meeting at Ball State. DePauw was set to host this year, but the school is currently undergoing a massive stadium renovation project that forced the administration to seek out neutral site options. top.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
top.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. I like to see myself as an actor. Nollywood is a starting point for me,” she said. The post I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Japan can be world's best, says outgoing coach Moriyasu
top.description: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 in a firendly in Singapore on Saturday (Roslan RAHMAN) Coach Hajime Moriyasu said Japan can become the best in the world after beating Brazil for a second time, as he prepares to step down after eight years in charge. Japan shocked the five-times world champions 3-2 in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday, with substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scoring an injury-time winner. The victory came just more than a year after Japan beat Brazil for the first time in a friendly in Tokyo. Brazil eliminated Japan from this year's World Cup in North America with a 2-1 win in the last 32. Moriyasu will leave his job after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday but he is certain that Japan are on track to become a major football nation. "The players showed confidence and courage and dug in when they needed to dig in," he said. "At the World Cup in the future, Japan can absolutely become the world's best." Moriyasu, Japan's longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa. But the Asian Football Confederation announced that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to "exceptional circumstances" in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country. The JFA confirmed on Friday that next week's game would be Moriyasu's last. "Aiming for wins and growth, I will strive to do my best as I always have," Moriyasu said. Japan were looking for revenge after a heart-breaking loss to Brazil at the World Cup. Gabriel Martinelli scored in the 95th minute in Houston to send Brazil through. Japan midfielder Ao Tanaka, who was in floods of tears after making a late mistake in the World Cup game, said after the win in Singapore that he was "calm but really happy". "All sorts of things started coming back to me as the game got closer, and of course those frustrating memories were in my head," said the Leeds United midfielder. Japan took an early 2-0 lead before Brazil hit back through two Vinicius Junior wonder strikes. Coventry winger Sakamoto won it for Japan in injury time, before Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were sent off for protesting the goal. The 30-year-old Sakamoto was making his first Japan appearance for five years. "To come back like this and make a contribution in such a massive match, one we all really wanted to win, gives me so much confidence," said Sakamoto. amk/tc

top.title: USMNT deliver six-goal statement in Mauricio Pochettino's penultimate match
top.description: USMNT deliver six-goal statement in Mauricio Pochettino's penultimate match By Ari Liljenwall Mauricio Pochettino's tenure with the US men's national team is nearing its conclusion, but he's making sure it ends with a flourish. With their head coach set to depart for Manchester United following Tuesday's second leg, the USMNT delivered a comprehensive performance on Saturday, dismantling Haiti 6-0 at Inter Miami 's Nu Stadium in the opening match of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal. Christian Pulisic struck twice, while Auston Trusty, Julian Hall , Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun also found the scoresheet as the USMNT turned a narrow halftime advantage into a rout, putting one foot in the Nations League semifinals. Final flourish The result came amid an unusual backdrop, as the team entered Saturday's match facing considerable uncertainty following the news of Pochettino's impending departure. The Argentine's decision to leave for Manchester United sent shockwaves through the program, coming just months after he signed a contract extension following the 2026 FIFA World Cup . Instead of building toward another cycle under Pochettino, the USMNT suddenly found themselves preparing for another coaching transition. But if the news threatened to become a distraction, it hardly showed on the field. The Yanks put the uncertainty aside and delivered one of the most dominant performances of Pochettino's tenure, giving their outgoing manager plenty to celebrate as he approaches his final match in charge. Rising star, established star Among the biggest individual standouts was the 18-year-old Hall, who continued his rapid ascent with another milestone moment on the international stage. The Manhattan native has enjoyed a breakout 2026 campaign with Red Bull New York , recording 13g/5a in 33 MLS appearances. He also became the youngest player in league history to net a hat trick and earned his first MLS All-Star selection. On Saturday, he scored his fourth international goal in five games with a composed finish in transition, adding another highlight to his burgeoning USMNT career and showcasing his growing importance to the program's next generation. Meanwhile, Christian Pulisic reminded everyone of his enduring value in his first match back with the squad since this summer's World Cup. The long-time US star delivered a brace that included a penalty kick and a spectacular individual strike from outside the penalty box. The AC Milan star's performance underscored the attacking quality at Pochettino's disposal, with nine separate players tallying a goal contribution on the evening. Last dance With a commanding six-goal advantage heading into Tuesday's return leg at FC Cincinnati 's TQL Stadium, the US are firmly in control of their Nations League quarterfinal tie. top.description: The Annika leader Lindy Duncan, right, hugs Carlota Ciganda at the 18th hole following Saturday's third round. top.title: Amateurs Waste Strokes On Seven Short-Game Myths
top.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Many golfers spend hours perfecting their full swing only to lose shots around the green due to outdated advice. A fresh analysis from MyGolfSpy breaks down seven specific myths that keep handicaps high. The report, updated for 2026, targets fundamental errors in bunker play, chipping, and wedge selection that plague amateurs from 35 to 65. These aren’t just minor tweaks; they are fundamental misconceptions that turn distance and spin into guesswork for players trying to lower their scores. The instruction industry has long passed down rules that don’t match how the game is actually played on tour. MyGolfSpy points out that players often exaggerate these techniques, leading to poor contact and low spin rates. The data suggests that sticking to rigid rules without understanding the physics of the clubface leads to costly mistakes. Golfers need to stop believing that one stance or one grip works for every lie around the green. The Bunker Stance Trap The first major myth involves the bunker setup. Many amateurs are told to “Open your stance in the bunker and swing along your feet.” MyGolfSpy notes that while an open stance is valid, exaggerating it causes the handle to drift ahead of the clubhead. This de-lofts the club, sending the ball out low with little spin. Tour players often use a more square setup to let the bounce work properly. If a player keeps the stance too open, the ball comes out uncontrollable. Aim more square to allow the clubhead to release toward the target. For long bunker shots, the advice to square a 60-degree wedge to make it go farther is also flawed. MyGolfSpy states, “For long bunker shots, square a 60-degree wedge to make it go farther.” This is a trap because a 52 or 54-degree wedge with an open face actually beats a squared 60-degree wedge for distance and control. Plugged Lies and Wrist Locks When the ball sits deep in the sand, the instinct to “Plugged lie? Close the face and chop it out” is dangerous. A plugged lie with a closed face launches the ball hot and uncontrollable. The report warns that this technique fails because the club cannot slide under the ball effectively. The source explicitly states, “Locking your wrists in the short game turns distance and spin into guesswork.” A gentle hinge on the way back and a soft release through are far better for consistency. Trying to hit the ball with a stiff wrist removes the necessary feel for the shot. nigeria.title: I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Nollywood actress Obioma Ofoegbu has spoken about the challenges of being stereotyped because of her plus-size physique, saying she is determined to establish herself as a versatile performer capable of taking on diverse roles. In an interview with Potpourri, Ofoegbu said she had repeatedly been offered roles that portrayed her as an older woman or confined her to characters typically associated with plus-size actresses. “My biggest challenge when I started was not being stereotyped because of my body type. A lot of times, they tried to give me roles just because I’m a plus-size woman. They would make me older in some movies or give me the same stories that a plus-size woman is expected to tell,” she said. The actress, who officially began her film career in 2020 after years of participating in stage plays and theatre productions during her school days, said she had rejected several roles in a bid to break away from such limitations. “I’m young. I don’t have to play an older woman or a married woman just because I’m plus-size. I don’t want to be placed in a box because of my looks, my appearance, or where I live,” she added. Speaking about her most challenging role, Ofoegbu identified her performance in Africa Magic’s series, The Low Priest, where she portrayed a villainous character who undergoes a transformation. She described the experience as physically demanding, revealing that she had to learn more Igbo, chant incantations and endure challenging filming conditions. The experience, she said, strengthened her confidence in her abilities and taught her that preparation and resilience could help her handle demanding characters. Despite her preference for diverse roles, Ofoegbu admitted that economic realities in Nigeria could make accepting stereotypical roles necessary, particularly for emerging actors trying to establish themselves financially. “I’m not a Funke Akindele yet. I’m not big enough to be producing as I please, so definitely I would take up those roles. I would grow as an actor, save, build and get my face out there,” she said. She also described acting as an uncertain source of income for emerging performers, advising actors to develop alternative income streams rather than depend entirely on film roles. On film promotion, the actress, who also has experience as an executive producer, maintained that actors should support projects they feature in but insisted that producers must have independent marketing strategies. Her long-term ambition, she said, is to have her work recognised beyond Africa and collaborate with filmmakers across different parts of the world. “I’m an actor, I’m not just a Nollywood actor. I like to see myself as an actor. Nollywood is a starting point for me,” she said. The post I don’t want to be stereotyped because of my looks – Obioma Ofoegbu appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: My appearance has helped with visibility, branding — DJ Pretty Smile
nigeria.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Sexy and beautiful Nigerian disc jockey, Onyinyechi Maureen Eneje, popularly known as DJ Pretty Smile, has admitted that her physical appearance has played a significant role in boosting her visibility and personal branding, even as she insists that talent and performance remain the key to sustaining a successful career. The beautiful DJ, who made the revelation in an interview with Potpourri, said her personality and appearance often attract people’s attention initially, but her ability to deliver behind the decks is what keeps them interested. According to her, being a woman in a male-dominated entertainment industry comes with its advantages in terms of visibility, but appearance alone cannot guarantee longevity in the profession. “I think people are first attracted to my personality and appearance, but what keeps them interested is my energy and ability to actually deliver behind the decks. Being a woman in a male-dominated space definitely makes people notice you, but looks alone cannot sustain a career. You have to be good at what you do,” she said. She added that although her appearance has contributed to her visibility and branding, she wants to be recognised primarily for her musical abilities and capacity to entertain audiences. “My appearance has definitely helped with visibility and branding, but I’ve always wanted people to remember me as DJ Pretty Smile, the DJ who can actually make a room move,” she added. Speaking on why she chose disc jockeying over singing or dancing, Eneje said her passion for music and its ability to influence people’s moods informed her decision to become a DJ. “I’ve always loved music and the way it can change people’s mood instantly. I chose DJing because I love being the person who controls that energy and creates an experience for people,” she explained. She further described disc jockeying as more than simply playing songs, noting that the profession requires an understanding of audiences, timing and the ability to establish a connection with people. “For me, it’s not just about playing songs; it’s about knowing what people want to hear, when they want to hear it, and creating that connection with the crowd. I also love the freedom and creativity that comes with DJing,” she said. nigeria.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
nigeria.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. nigeria.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
nigeria.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. nigeria.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
nigeria.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway. The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. business.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. This created unnecessary friction, and I found myself having to mediate whenever issues arose, even though the service I had been engaged to provide was recruitment. I eventually had a lengthy conversation with one of the founders, explaining that communicating reporting lines and responsibilities during recruitment was only one part of the process. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is not a trend that can be reversed. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. sports.title: Pulisic Scores Twice As USMNT Crushes Haiti 6-0
sports.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images Christian Pulisic scored two goals in just two minutes to push the United States men’s national team to a dominant 6-0 victory over Haiti on Saturday night. The win came in Miami during the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals, marking the biggest rout of Mauricio Pochettino’s two years leading the squad. This result sets up a formality for the return leg in Cincinnati on Tuesday, where the current coach will take charge for the very last time. The buildup to this series carried heavy weight because Pochettino is leaving after only three months of a new four-year contract to become the manager of Manchester United, according to ESPN . Players showed no signs of distraction despite the looming change in leadership. Auston Trusty, who scored the opening goal from a corner kick in the 10th minute, spoke to TNT about the team’s focus on their departing coach. “We played for him,” Trusty told TNT. “Obviously he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. Obviously it’s a great opportunity that he is moving on into, but we play for him. It’s his team, it’s his identity.” Trusty also noted that the mindset remains to win every single game and keep fighting no matter how large the lead becomes. Pulisic returned to action for the first time since suffering an injury during a round-of-16 exit at the World Cup. Fourth on the team’s all-time leading scorers list, he surpassed Eric Wynalda thanks to his two second-half strikes. Five goals followed in a one-sided second half, with Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun rounding out the scoring alongside a fourth goal from teenager Julian Hall. Hall netted his fourth goal in just five appearances, a game that officially cap-tied him to the U.S. after he was previously eligible to represent Poland. A Final Sendoff in Miami Haiti was technically the home team for Saturday match, but the fixture moved to Miami due to ongoing gang violence in the Caribbean nation. The U.S. players executed a plan that left the opposition with little chance to respond, proving that the team can perform at a high level even when the coaching future remains uncertain. Next March, the Nations League semifinals and final are set to occur, with the U.S. under a yet-to-be-named new coach. While the team celebrates this massive win, attention shifts quickly to the search for the next leader. The United States Soccer Federation is reportedly pursuing Pep Guardiola aggressively, as initial negotiations are anticipated to begin next week. Since resigning as Manchester City’s manager in May 2026, Guardiola has been a highly-coveted free agent after securing 41 trophies over his 19 years managing in Europe. sports.title: Lincoln Riley drives USC insane with another loss. It's time to pull plug | Opinion
sports.description: What's the defintion of insanity? Well, it's Southern California. Because the Trojans keep doing the same thing over and over, expecting different results. In a result that has become an annual tradition, No. 14 USC lost another ranked game in November that has spoiled its hopes of the College Football Playoff . The 2026 edition of coach Lincoln Riley's tenure featured another mistake-riddled affair, blowing it against Indiana in a 27-13 loss . Riley is now just 6-15 in ranked games with the Trojans, including 1-9 on the road with the lone victory coming in his first season in 2022. Feeling insane yet? No matter how much talent he acquires or how the table is set perfectly for him, Riley continuously falls short in the games he not only is expected to win, but has to. No one cares he is 36-6 when facing unranked teams. When you're at USC, you're supposed to win the big games, and when you don't, that's when it's time for the bags to start being packed. USC was facing an Indiana team that hasn't been able to move the ball for over a month, and let backup quarterback Grant Wilson − making his first start since he was at Old Dominion in 2024 − throw for 305 yards and two touchdowns, opening up a battle at quarterback for the Hoosiers. It was the most points Indiana had scored since early October. Indiana has one of the best defenses in the country, but the loaded Trojans offense was meant to break it down just like how it did against Ohio State. Instead, USC was limited to just 13 points, and with Jayden Maiava throwing a season-high three interceptions, including in the red zone as the Trojans were on the cusp of tying the game late in the fourth quarter. USC also had both of its kickers miss a field goal. Once again, Riley's team completely implodes when the light at brightest. USC earned some credit back when it beat Ohio State on Halloween night , but that wasn't the end of it. sports.title: How Ball State gave DePauw and Wabash another successful Monon Bell game
sports.description: MUNCIE — In a game defined by the defenses, it was only fitting that the 132nd edition of the Monon Bell Classic came down to a clutch interception. With nine seconds left on the clock, Wabash quarterback Jackson Gilbert took the snap, dropped back, and launched a pass to the back left corner of the end zone for wide receiver Luke Adams. DePauw defensive back Joey Fico was there, though, and he leapt high into the air to snag the interception and seal a 16-10 victory for the Tigers at Ball State's Scheumann Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. "We've been practicing it all week," Fico said. "Not the pick, but the coverages. We knew that (Adams) was their guy, we got into a deep-third coverage, I saw him lined up one-on-one across from me. Their guy on our guy, I knew the ball was going to come up, and I was like, 'It's got to be me.' "I got up, did what I did, and the rest is history." As Fico came crashing down to the turf, the raucous crowd of DePauw fans and students that had filled up Ball State's bleachers erupted with thunderous cheers as the Tigers clinched their fifth-straight win over their archrival Little Giants. "You can't go to any other D-III school like Wabash and DePauw and get the support you get," Fico said. "I want to say a big thanks to all my friends and family that showed up because it does mean something. I definitely do play harder when there's a bunch of people out in front, knowing that they're supporting me." The Monon Bell Classic is not just the best Division III college football rivalry. It is considered by many to be the greatest rivalry the sport has to offer, no matter what level, and is one of the most historic rivalries in all of American sports, dating all the way back to 1890. With the two schools located just 27 miles apart in western Indiana — Wabash in Crawfordsville and DePauw in Greencastle — the rivaling rosters are often composed of high school teammates or even relatives. More: DePauw outlasts Wabash in 132nd Monon Bell game | Final score, highlights The Monon Bell itself — a 300-pound locomotive bell taken from the Monon Railroad — was introduced as a traveling trophy in 1932 and has famously been stolen by students from each school on nine different occasions. The famous Bell made its way through the procession of DePauw tailgaters that flooded the Scheumann Stadium parking lot before the game, and DePauw staffers and students rang it loudly and proudly before, during and after the game. How Ball State became the host for the 2026 Monon Bell Classic From 1915 until 1922, the rivalry game was held at neutral sites to accommodate larger crowds and alumni. The 1922 meeting at Irwin Field in Indianapolis marked the last time that the game was played at a neutral site until this year's meeting at Ball State. DePauw was set to host this year, but the school is currently undergoing a massive stadium renovation project that forced the administration to seek out neutral site options. sports.title: Japan can be world's best, says outgoing coach Moriyasu
sports.description: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 in a firendly in Singapore on Saturday (Roslan RAHMAN) Coach Hajime Moriyasu said Japan can become the best in the world after beating Brazil for a second time, as he prepares to step down after eight years in charge. Japan shocked the five-times world champions 3-2 in a friendly in Singapore on Saturday, with substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scoring an injury-time winner. The victory came just more than a year after Japan beat Brazil for the first time in a friendly in Tokyo. Brazil eliminated Japan from this year's World Cup in North America with a 2-1 win in the last 32. Moriyasu will leave his job after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday but he is certain that Japan are on track to become a major football nation. "The players showed confidence and courage and dug in when they needed to dig in," he said. "At the World Cup in the future, Japan can absolutely become the world's best." Moriyasu, Japan's longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa. But the Asian Football Confederation announced that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to "exceptional circumstances" in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country. The JFA confirmed on Friday that next week's game would be Moriyasu's last. "Aiming for wins and growth, I will strive to do my best as I always have," Moriyasu said. Japan were looking for revenge after a heart-breaking loss to Brazil at the World Cup. Gabriel Martinelli scored in the 95th minute in Houston to send Brazil through. Japan midfielder Ao Tanaka, who was in floods of tears after making a late mistake in the World Cup game, said after the win in Singapore that he was "calm but really happy". "All sorts of things started coming back to me as the game got closer, and of course those frustrating memories were in my head," said the Leeds United midfielder. Japan took an early 2-0 lead before Brazil hit back through two Vinicius Junior wonder strikes. Coventry winger Sakamoto won it for Japan in injury time, before Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti and captain Raphinha were sent off for protesting the goal. The 30-year-old Sakamoto was making his first Japan appearance for five years. "To come back like this and make a contribution in such a massive match, one we all really wanted to win, gives me so much confidence," said Sakamoto. amk/tc

The instruction industry has long passed down rules that don’t match how the game is actually played on tour. MyGolfSpy points out that players often exaggerate these techniques, leading to poor contact and low spin rates. The data suggests that sticking to rigid rules without understanding the physics of the clubface leads to costly mistakes. Many amateurs are told to “Open your stance in the bunker and swing along your feet.” MyGolfSpy notes that while an open stance is valid, exaggerating it causes the handle to drift ahead of the clubhead. This de-lofts the club, sending the ball out low with little spin. Tour players often use a more square setup to let the bounce work properly. If a player keeps the stance too open, the ball comes out uncontrollable. Aim more square to allow the clubhead to release toward the target. sports.title: Ryan Conwell Proves Heat Found Gold In Second-Round Pick
sports.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Ryan Conwell just dropped 20 points on the Cleveland Cavaliers, and that performance changes the whole conversation about Miami’s backcourt. This rookie is not just filling time; he is making plays when the team needs them most. Sun Sentinel ‘s Ira Winderman notes that Conwell has emerged as a valuable second-round selection for the franchise. The numbers back up the hype from Friday night. Conwell finished with five rebounds while shooting 6-for-12 from the field and 4-for-9 from deep against the Cavs, per All U Can Heat . His last four games show a player on the rise, averaging 11 points and hitting 40 percent of his threes. The Heat went 3-1 during this specific stretch, proving the rookie’s impact on the win column. A Scorer When Others Are Out Heat fans know how thin the roster gets when injuries pile up. Pelle Larsson and Klay Thompson sat out the Friday night victory, leaving a massive hole in the lineup. Conwell stepped in and logged 33 minutes, playing more than any Heat player aside from Bam Adebayo and Davion Mitchell, according to All U Can Heat. That heavy workload shows exactly how much the coaching staff trusts him right now. But there is a clear difference between Conwell and other options. Sun Sentinel reporter Ira Winderman noted that comparing Conwell to Kasparas Jakucionis is somewhat apples to oranges. Jakucionis is more of a point guard, while Conwell operates as an undersized scorer who can create his own shot. This distinction matters because Miami needs someone who can score when the defense collapses. Depth Issues Still Loom Large Even with a strong showing, the team faces a tough reality about its backcourt. Ira Winderman highlighted that insufficient depth at the point guard spot continues to be a major concern for Miami. During Friday’s matchup, Erik Spoelstra faced significant difficulty resting Davion Mitchell, while Dru Smith contributed little in his short appearance. The truth is that the Heat likely require point guard depth more than in any other area. The story of how Conwell landed in Miami adds another layer to his value. Per Sun Sentinel, he resulted from a compensatory second-round pick the Heat obtained from the Hornets because they were not informed about the gambling investigation depth concerning Terry Rozier before the trade. That pick turned into a player who arrived exactly when needed. Some fans might compare his future value to the first-round pick the Hornets still hold from the Rozier trade, which is top-14 protected in June and otherwise unprotected in 2028, according to reports. That potential future asset highlights just how valuable a current contributor like Conwell can be. A more fitting comparison for Ryan could be whatever asset the Hornets eventually acquire from that first-round selection.

science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 13, 1971: NASA's Mariner 9 becomes 1st spacecraft to orbit Mars, revealing close looks at the Martian surface
science.description: null On Nov. 13, 1971, Mariner 9 became the first spacecraft to orbit Mars. At the time, scientists didn't know much about the Red Planet. NASA had several Mars flybys before Mariner 9 . Those flybys showed that Mars had a cratered surface , so some scientists thought that Mars looked just like the moon. Then Mariner 9 blew blew their minds. When Mariner 9 got to Mars , it arrived in the middle of a dust storm. It saw some tall structures sticking through the clouds. When the dust settled, images from Mariner 9 revealed that these structures were the tops of huge volcanoes. One volcano, Olympus Mons , is the tallest in the solar system. Mariner 9 also spotted an enormous canyon called Valles Marineris . This canyon is five times longer than the Grand Canyon in Arizona. Mariner 9 worked for one year in orbit. When it ran out of gas, NASA shut it off. But the spacecraft remains one of the most famous Mars voyagers of all time. The Mariner 9 spacecraft, seen here in a NASA model, was the first to orbit Mars in 1971. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered Mariner 9 cemented its place in space history when it entered into orbit around Mars, the first human-built spacecraft ever to do so. The NASA spacecraft actually beat the Soviet Union's own Mars 2 spacecraft to the Red Planet, even though Mars 2 "had an 11-day head start," NASA said in a mission description . (Mars 2 would go on to be the first human-built craft to impact the surface of Mars when it crashed into the Red Planet.) But it was the science from Mariner 9 that transformed Mars from a mysterious Red Planet into a full world for humans to explore. The Boldest Mars Missions in History The Mariner 9 mission first saw the peak of Olympus Mons on Mars in the midst of a global dust storm in 1971. (Image credit: NASA/JPL) Mariner 9 carried four primary instruments to study Mars, including a camera system for imaging, an ultraviolet spectrometer, an infrared spectrometer and an infrared radiometer. The probe mapped 85% of Mars with those tools during its nearly one-year mission. The Mariner 9 spacecraft discovered 20 giant volcanoes on Mars (including Olympus Mars) and made key observations to map Valles Marineris, which runs 2,500 miles (4,000 kilometers) long acros the Tharsis region and is 120 miles (200 km) wide. "The canyon was named in honor of Mariner 9," NASA said in an overview . In all, Mariner 9 took 7,329 photos of the surface of Mars, mapping the planet down to a resolution of between 1/2-1 mile (1-2 km). It also snapped at least 80 photos of Phobos and Deimos, the two small moons of Mars. By February 1972, Mariner 9's supply of gaseous nitrogen, which it used to feed its attitide control thrusters, had run dry. NASA finally shut down the mission in October 1972.
